newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA says Australia wage rises under control.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA says Australia wage rises under control.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) retiring governor Bernie Fraser said on Thursday wage increases were under control for the time being.
"Central bankers always worry about wage increases," Fraser told a parliamentary committee hearing.

"But the fact that we lowered interest rates a short time ago, the fact that we're talking about the inflation rate coming comfortably back within out two to three percent (target range) indicates that at least for the time being we think that wage increases are under control."
"So, at this point in time, we are not worried about any particular claim as such, it's the outcomes that are going to be important," Fraser told the hearing on the bank's annual report.
Australia's Liberal-National government has forecast average earnings to increase 5.0 percent in the fiscal year to June 30, 1997, from 4.0 percent in 1995/96.
The Treasury said in the 1996/97 budget that wages pressures were not expected to intensify over the year, but that they needed continued policy vigilance.
The Reserve Bank has previously expressed concern that the level of annual wage increases should not exceed 4.5 percent to avoid threatening low inflation.
